These two appeals are preferred by accused Nos.2 and 7 respectively in Crime No.241/2016 and Crime No.258/2015, registered at Mandya West Police Station for the offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC.

sentences.text: The appellants preferred Crl.Misc.No.965/2023 in Crime No.241/2016 and Crl.Misc.No.966/2023 in Crime No.258/2015 before the learned Sessions Judge, under Section 438 of Cr.P.C., to enlarge them on anticipatory bail.
3. The learned Sessions Judge vide order dated 22.01.2024 dismissed Crl.Misc.No.965/2023 and vide order dated 23.01.2024 dismissed Crl.Misc.No.966/2023.

4. The allegations in Crime No.241/2016 are that on 10.12.2008, Directors of PACL, India Private Limited, Mandya and it's advisers gave publicity that the said company was established for the welfare of the poor and if any amount is deposited, the depositors will get double the amount in five to seven years.

It is alleged that, on an assurance that the amount will be returned as assured on it's maturity, the complainant by name Radha deposited a total sum of Rs.33,120/- and similarly one Smt. B.N. Bhagya deposited a NC: 2024:KHC:10689 sum of Rs.33,120/-, one Mahadevi deposited Rs.23,040/- and one Vanitha K.C. deposited a sum of Rs.15,000/-.

It is alleged that, even after the maturity and surrendering the original bond, the accused without returning the amount as assured,
cheated the complainant and other persons.

5. Similar allegations are made in Crime No.258/2015 that on 01.08.20208, Directors of PACL,
India Private Limited, Mandya and it's advisers came to the complainant's village, Gurudevnahalli and gave publicity that the said company was established for the welfare of the poor and if any amount is deposited, the depositors will get double the amount in five to seven years.
It is alleged that, on an assurance that the amount will be returned as assured on it's maturity, the complainant by name Sudha.

S.N. deposited a total sum of Rs.1,500/- and similarly some other villagers such as G.K.Sumithra D/o Krishna deposited a total sum of Rs.7,680/-, Suvarnambika W/o Boregowda deposited a total sum of Rs.30,000/-, Smt. Sheela W/o Kantharaju deposited a total sum of Rs.15,000/-, Sri. Abhishek S/o Boregowda deposited a total sum of Rs.15,000/- and also one Smt.
Rathnamma W/o A.M. Nagaraju deposited a total sum of Rs.14,400/-.
It is NC: 2024:KHC:10689 alleged that, even after the maturity and surrendering the original bond, the accused without returning the amount as assured, cheated the complainant and other persons.
6. The learned High Court Government Pleader has contended that there are totally 76 cases registered against the accused persons all over India.

The accused have cheated the depositors by inducing them to deposit the amount on an assurance that the amount will be doubled in 5-7 years,
but later cheated them without returning any amount even after it's maturity.
He has contended that the appellants are required for custodial interrogation as they have cheated several persons to the tune of more than Rs.32,00,000/-.

He has contended that the investigation is still under progress and therefore, if the appellants are granted the relief they have sought in this appeal, they may not co-operate with the investigation of the case.

He further contended that during the course of investigation, Section 9 of the KPIDFE Act has been invoked and hence, the appellants are not entitled for anticipatory bail.
7.

The learned Sessions Judge while dismissing the petition seeking anticipatory bail, has observed that though FIR is registered only for the offence under Section 420 of IPC, the NC:
2024:KHC:10689 Investigation Officer has invoked Section 9 of the KPIDEF Act and Section 406 Mr. Subrata Bhattacharya vs State Of Karnataka on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9921012/
4 and 409 of IPC with the leave of the Court, as per the objections filed by the learned Public Prosecutor.

sentences.text: Hence, the learned Sessions Judge has dismissed the petition filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C observing that a petition under Section 438 of Cr.P.C., is not maintainable in view of the bar contained under Section 18(2) of the Act and only an appeal lies to the High Court against the orders passed by the Special Court as incorporated under Section 16 of the said Act.

8. The learned counsel for the appellants has brought to the notice of the Court that in the main case registered by the CBI, FIR No.RC-BD1/2014/E0004-CBI/BS&FC/New Delhi dated 19.02.2014, the appellants are enlarged on bail.

A copy of the order passed by the Special Judge (PC ACT), (CBI)-16,
RADC dated 25.10.2023 has been produced at annexure E to the petition.

9. The Court of Principal City Civil and Sessions Judge at Bengaluru, in Crl.Misc.No.10535/2023 vide order dated 27.12.2023 has granted anticipatory bail to the appellants in connection with Crime No.291/2013 registered at Rajagopalanagar Police Station, wherein, charge sheet is filed NC:
2024:KHC:10689 against them for the offence punishable under Section 418, 409, 420, 120B read with Section 34 of IPC, Section 4 to 6 of Price Chits and Money Circulation Scheme (Banning) Act 1978 and Section 9 of the KPIDFE Act.

sentences.text: 10. The allegations are that, the accused have induced the complainants and similar other persons to deposit money in their company with an assurance that the said money will be doubled in 5-7 years and later failed to return the amount as assured and thereby cheated them.
FIR was initially registered for offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC.
In the course of investigation, Section 406 and 409 and Section 9 of the KPIDFE Act are said to be invoked.
In similar cases registered against the appellants as notes supra, they have been enlarged on bail.

11. One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel is that the appellants are nowhere concerned to the alleged transactions between the complainant and the company and they are not the beneficiaries nor the share holders of the company.
12. The accusation made against the appellants need to be proved during the Trial of the case.
The offences alleged are NC: 2024:KHC:10689 not punishable with death or imprisonment for life.
Considering the entire facts and circumstances, the relief sought in the appeal can be granted by imposing necessary conditions.

Hence, the following:
ORDER i) Crl.A.No.292/2024 and Crl.A.No.190/2024 are allowed.

ii) The order dated 22.01.2024 passed in Crl.Misc.No.965/2023 and dated 23.01.2024 passed in Crl.Misc.No.966/2023 by the Court of the Principal District and Sessions Judge at Mandya are set aside subject to following conditions:
